solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; the grid proves the blog's enumeration wrong at 14 down, recounted from the answer here

clue.text: Rat in river for some years

indicators.note: the word in tells us the rat sits inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a rat or cad is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rodent spotted in a river over a period of several years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' is not the animal but a person who behaves badly, a cad. The Dee is a river in Scotland and another in England and Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: A decade is a span of ten years, so it is a fair way to say some years.

clue.text: Sweet daughter is not with Yankee

parts.note: ain't is colloquial for is not
Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A sweet-natured daughter is not keen on an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dainty is delicate and pretty, which is what sweet often means of small things.

clue.text: Turn up with a band in high spirits

parts.note: to cock something is to tilt it upwards, as with a hat brim or an ear
a hoop is a circular band

explanation.surface: Someone arrives with a group of musicians, cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' looks like musicians but is a ring of metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cock-a-hoop means jubilant or elated, especially about a triumph.

clue.text: Spirit shown in March and November

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A ghost appears in two months of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: March and November read as months, but March is a protest demonstration and November gives N.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon is an evil supernatural being, a malevolent spirit.

clue.text: Court stops A4e having effect

indicators.note: to stop something is to plug it, so the court abbreviation fills a gap in the other letters

parts.note: A as written, 4 in Roman numerals as IV, then e as written

explanation.surface: A court case halts the welfare firm A4e from taking effect.
explanation.walkthrough: A4e was a British welfare-to-work company, but here it is just A, IV (Roman 4) and E, with CT stopping the gap after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Something active is in operation and producing results, which is what having effect means.

clue.text: Monster to agree with artist

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree with it
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword staple for artist

explanation.surface: A beast says it agrees with a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimera of Greek myth was a fire-breathing beast that was part lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: Princess visiting Trinidad

indicators.note: a visitor is inside a place, so the answer sits within the island's name

explanation.surface: A royal princess on a visit to the Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: Princess Ida is the heroine of a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is the title princess of the Gilbert and Sullivan opera Princess Ida.

clue.text: One hug could be sufficient

indicators.note: could be hints that these letters might become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A single cuddle might be all that is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough means as much as is needed, a plain synonym for adequate or sufficient.

clue.text: Funny man in comic duo beyond contact

indicators.note: funny can mean odd or peculiar, a hint that the following letters are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: The amusing member of a comedy double act is out of reach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny man' reads as a comedian, but 'Funny' is the anagram signal working on all of MAN IN COMIC DUO.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone held incommunicado cannot be reached or spoken to, so they are out of contact.

clue.text: Bore in a French river

parts.note: un is French for a
the Derwent is a river in England

explanation.surface: A tedious person is in a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' is the past tense of bear (endure), not a dull person. The Derwent is an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: To have undergone something is to have endured it, so underwent is the past tense matching bore.

clue.text: Two tons taken by old farm wagon

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm cart or wagon

explanation.surface: A couple of tons of produce loaded on an old farm cart.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is an archaic word meaning a pair, as in 'never the twain shall meet'.

clue.text: Trying to get round figure reduced?

definitions.text: Trying to get round figure reduced?

parts.words: Trying to get round figure reduced?
parts.note: the whole clue describes someone cutting back food to slim a rounded body; 'round figure' also suggests a number being rounded down

explanation.walkthrough: A 'round figure' sounds like a number to be rounded off, but it is a plump body that someone is attempting to slim.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting down on food is the usual way a person tries to make a portly body slimmer.

clue.text: College group some distance beneath climber

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece beneath another comes after it

parts.note: ivy is a climbing plant
a league is an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: A university group stands some way below a climber.
explanation.walkthrough: The climber is a plant, not a mountaineer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ivy League is the group of eight elite universities in the north-east United States.

clue.text: Even a dory somehow can be prepared for roasting

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters get there by some unspecified rearrangement

explanation.surface: Even a dory, the fish, can be got ready for the oven one way or another.
explanation.walkthrough: A dory is a sea fish, which makes the cooking surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: Supermarket food described as oven-ready is already prepped so it can go straight in to cook.

clue.text: Narcissists say it's so messed up

parts.note: e.g. means for example, which say also signals

indicators.note: messed up means jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Self-obsessed people, you might say, have it all wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoists think chiefly of themselves, as narcissists do in their self-love.

clue.text: Almost have chat about flying saucer

indicators.note: almost means the word falls just short of complete, its final letter dropped

parts.note: to discuss is to talk something over

explanation.surface: People nearly start talking about a UFO.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying saucer' suggests a UFO, but it describes the athletics disc thrown through the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is a heavy disc thrown in athletics, a saucer-shaped object sent flying.

clue.text: Commercial opening is coming

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a vent is an opening or outlet

explanation.surface: An advert's launch is on its way.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means an arrival, the coming of something or someone important.

clue.text: Little rascal learning to beg

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
lore is knowledge or learning handed down

explanation.surface: A naughty child picks up knowledge so as to plead.
explanation.definitionFit: To implore someone is to plead with them earnestly, a stronger synonym for beg.

clue.text: Poor holding on for money

indicators.note: holding means the first word grips the second inside it

parts.note: poor quality means bad
re means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A poor person clings on to get some money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is slang for money, from the idea of earning one's daily bread.

clue.text: Dull Soviet spy

definitions.meaning: a ... blade is dull, not sharp
Anthony ..., art historian, spied for the Soviet Union in the Cambridge spy ring

explanation.walkthrough: Anthony Blunt was one of the Cambridge Five, British establishment figures who passed secrets to Moscow.
explanation.definitionFit: A knife without an edge is blunt or dull; Anthony Blunt was the notorious Cambridge spy.

clue.text: Students have trouble in Marxist concept

parts.note: a class is a group of students
to struggle is to have difficulty

explanation.surface: Pupils find a piece of Marxist theory hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: In Marx's theory, history is driven by conflict between social classes, workers against owners.

clue.text: Beer reportedly makes you sicken

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard or told, so we want a word that sounds like the beer

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Drinking beer, people say, makes you ill.
explanation.definitionFit: To ail is to be unwell or to fall ill, which is what sicken means intransitively.

clue.text: Trumpet has place in window

indicators.note: in says the place abbreviation goes inside the window word

parts.note: a sash is a sliding window frame
PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

explanation.surface: A trumpet player has a spot in the window.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trumpet' is a verb here: to proclaim loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To splash a story is to display it prominently, as a newspaper headline does, much like trumpeting it.

clue.text: Setter barking shows the way

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazily out of order

explanation.surface: A barking setter, the dog, leads the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is a gun dog, and 'barking' (British slang for crazy) is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is a road, and 'way' is used in road names in the same sense.
